core_obligations: Reduce, as in the codimension one case, to X = Spec(A) with A a domain and Y = Spec(B) with B a Noetherian local domain contained in A after dividing out the kernel of B to A (proof lines 3681-3685).

Apply the dimension formula to obtain dim(O_{X,x}) + trdeg_{kappa(y)} kappa(x) <= dim(B) + trdeg_B(A), and identify trdeg_B(A) with d via the fibre dimension at the generic point (proof lines 3686-3694).

Use that the local ring at x is a Noetherian domain mapping onto the local ring of the fibre with nonzero kernel, because the generic point does not map to y, to deduce dim(O_{X,x}) > dim(O_{X_y,x}); combining the two inequalities gives dim_x(X_y) < dim(B) + d as required (proof lines 3695-3705).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the affine domain case (proof lines 3681-3685).
Use the strict inequality of local ring dimensions (proof lines 3695-3705).
difficulty_reason: For f: X to Y locally of finite type, a point x whose image y has Noetherian local ring, and an integer d equal to the fibre dimension at every generic point of an irreducible component of X through x which does not map to y, the lemma bounds dim_x(X_y) by d + dim(O_{Y,y}) - 1 (statement lines 3670-3678). The proof copies the reduction of the codimension one case to reduce to X = Spec(A) with A a domain and Y = Spec(B) with B a Noetherian local domain contained in A (proof lines 3681-3685). The dimension formula then gives an inequality between dim(O_{X,x}) plus a transcendence degree on the left and dim(B) plus the transcendence degree of A over B on the right, where the latter is exactly d by hypothesis; since the local ring at x maps onto the local ring of the fibre with a nonzero kernel and is a Noetherian domain, its dimension is strictly larger than the fibre dimension upstairs, and the two comparisons produce the stated strict bound (proof lines 3686-3706). The claim is H2: the same two ingredients as the codimension one case with the strict inequality now bounding rather than identifying the fibre dimension.
